summary: Deletes a file and normalizes the result into a simple success/failure code. Calls DeleteFileA(lpFileName); on success the local error code is set to 0, otherwise it is set to GetLastError(). If the resulting code is zero the function returns 0 (success). Otherwise the failure code is passed to ErrorIDLookupTable(LastError) (an error-code to message/lookup handler) and the function returns -1. A thin Win32 wrapper used by six callers including vehicle scene/tire loading, setting-existence checks and physics joint loading paths.

local_names.lpFileName: name or path of the file to delete
local_names.LastError: Windows last-error code captured when DeleteFileA fails

operations.description: DeleteFileA(lpFileName) attempts to delete the named file via the Win32 DeleteFileA import.
If DeleteFileA returned non-zero the deletion succeeded and LastError is set to 0; otherwise LastError is set to GetLastError() to capture the failure code.
If LastError is zero the function returns 0 immediately, signalling success.
ErrorIDLookupTable(LastError) consumes the non-zero failure code (error-code to message lookup/handler).
Return -1 to signal that the deletion failed.

unresolved: The behavior of ErrorIDLookupTable is not evidenced by this packet; whether it logs, shows an error dialog, or maps the code into a user-visible message is unknown.
The success/failure convention (0 on success, -1 on failure) is stated by the raw source but the meaning callers attach to it is not evidenced here.
The GetLastError import's read is the only use of the 0x0059E188 global in this function; its runtime state is not captured by the packet.
